s1.syndrome_frame: Neurocutaneous disorder with seizures and multiple congenital anomalies
salient_findings: Massive neoplasm formation in posterior cranial fossa
key_facts: Patient is a 12-month-old boy
Presented with convulsive seizures
Seizures characterized by faltering, smirking with withdrawal of the head and eyes
Had a blond hair strand at birth
Had polydactyly of the right hand at birth
Had cardiac rhabdomyoma at birth
Depigmented spots appeared on torso at 4 months
First convulsive seizures noted at 8 months
Psychomotor development was normal for age
No family history of similar conditions
Brain CT scan showed massive neoplasm formation in posterior cranial fossa
Brain MRI with contrast revealed extracranial solid mass in posterior fossa with brain stem compression
Genetic testing revealed TSC1 gene mutation

shortlist.label: Tuberous Sclerosis Complex
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has TSC1 gene mutation, cardiac rhabdomyoma, depigmented spots, and subcortical tubers, which are characteristic features of TSC

shortlist.label: Subependymal Giant Cell Astrocytoma
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a massive neoplasm formation in the posterior cranial fossa and a TSC1 gene mutation, which increases the likelihood of SEGA

shortlist.label: Neurofibromatosis Type 1
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has multiple congenital anomalies and seizures, which can be seen in NF1, although the presence of a TSC1 gene mutation makes TSC more likely

shortlist.label: Sturge-Weber Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has depigmented spots and seizures, which can be seen in SWS, although the presence of a TSC1 gene mutation and other features makes TSC more likely

shortlist.label: Hemimegalencephaly
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has seizures and a large epithelioid cell tumor, which can be seen in HME, although the presence of a TSC1 gene mutation and other features makes TSC more likely
